assumptions: The paper does not name the estimator; ordinary least squares is used as a best-effort interpretation of its firm-level time-series regression.
The paper does not date the denominators for lagged and leading CFO; each CFO observation uses average assets for its own fiscal year.
The current local COMP.FUNDA vintage is translated to the paper's industrial/research population using INDL, STD, C, and D filters.
The item 123 earnings input is IBC (`ibc`); pooled SAS 1st/99th percentile cutoffs use scaled CFO, item-123 earnings (Prof), and signed ΔWC.

Each average-assets denominator is available only when both source years have the same known CURCD; no CURRTR conversion is applied because the provider description does not specify arithmetic direction.

The p. 8 prose requiring past/future cash flows and earnings is interpreted as requiring CFO and constructed Earn (CFO + ΔWC) at t−1 and t+1; Table 1's row labels only lead/lag CFO, so this is a documented source ambiguity.
Lead/lag CFO and Earn use raw adjacent fiscal-year records, including 1986/2000 where needed for 1987/1999 outcomes; neighboring rows need not independently survive current-year trimming.
Cross-firm t-statistics use the sample standard deviation of firm coefficients and N−1 degrees of freedom.

limitations: The paper does not explicitly specify the individual-fit estimator, the denominator date for lagged/leading CFO, which earnings series is screened at leads/lags or trimmed (Prof vs constructed Earn), or percentile interpolation. The page 8 sample prose and Table 1 lead/lag row differ; the selected screen follows the broader prose.
The current local Compustat vintage and modern population filters are not confirmed to recreate the historical Compustat research file population.

The paper does not specify currency handling. Unlike-currency or unknown-CURCD average-assets denominators are unavailable because the local provider description of CURRTR does not establish conversion direction or use for these annual constructions.
